1.2K views · 23 reactions | A promise of lucrative employment abroad allegedly ended in forced prostitution, severe beatings and human trafficking for a 21-year-old Nigerian woman rescued from Mali by operatives of the Nigeria Police Force. Identified as Godiya Amos, a pseudonym, the victim was reportedly lured from Akwanga, Nasarawa State, and sold to members of an international trafficking network for CFA 420,000, equivalent to approximately ₦770,000. Police investigations led to the arrest of three suspected members of the syndicate, while the rescued woman reportedly disclosed that about 42 other Nigerian women remained trapped in a makeshift camp within a remote gold-mining settlement in Mali. The police say investigations are ongoing, with efforts to apprehend other members of the network and secure the rescue of the remaining victims. The case highlights the dangers of deceptive overseas employment offers and the continuing threat of cross-border human trafficking.
